newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges U.N. to speed up oil deal implementation.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges U.N. to speed up oil deal implementation.

text.p: Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammad Saeed al-Sahaf has urged the United Nations to speed up the implementation of the second phase of its oil-for-food deal, the Iraqi News Agency INA said on Wednesday.

INA said Sahaf, in a letter to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, also accused the United States and Britain of impeding the application of the oil pact by putting on hold several food and medical contracts.
"I hope that the implementation of the new phase will be quick and that food supplies will reach Iraq within the second six months (of the deal)," Sahaf said.

The oil-for-food deal, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, went into effect last December and was renewed for another six months on June 8. But Iraq had delayed exports for the second phase to modify the plans for aid.
Iraqi newspapers said that Baghdad would resume its oil exports under the deal on Wednesday.
Iraq has frequently complained about the slow transfer of food and medicines purchased under the deal, blaming the delay on the United States and Britain.
United Nations officials in Baghdad said on Sunday that 1.5 million tonnes of food out of the 2.3 million Iraq planned to buy in the first six months of the deal had reached the country.

"Although two months have ended since the end of the first phase, the (U.N. sanctions) committee has not been able to approve 142 contracts worth $87 million because of the United States and Britain...," Sahaf said
"You (Annan) have noticed...the size of difficulties and obstacles which were and still put by...the United States and Britain."
He said the United States and Britain were also delaying 60 other contracts worth $18 million and had rejected 15 others with a total value of $70 million from the first stage of the pact.
Iraq said on Tuesday the U.S. representative at the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq rejected a contract with a French firm to buy 100 ambulances.
Sahaf urged Annan to intervene in order to approve the 142 contracts and others as soon as possible, INA said.
